items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Well, Glenn Wilson, the new clarinet player in town... [INTERVIEWEE] Was he playing saxophone at the time?

ctx.x: Well, as I mentioned before, I started out playing dance music and all the dance bands, well they played the regular orchestrations that you would go by at Whirline's or any of the music stores. And occasionally during the night you would fake a few tunes, you know, play some jazz, but 80% of it was reading the regular orchestrations because 90% of the work you would get was for dancing, you see. But we would throw in a few fake tunes without doing any reading at all and just kind of jazz it up a little during…

Well, some of the players I was listening to yesterday with Connie Jones, I thought they were very smooth. Well, Glenn Wilson, the new clarinet player in town, talking about him. And he'll play very smoothly for a while and then he'll play some really dirty notes, some rough style playing once in a while just to maybe lend a little variety or something. Well, that's possible.
Was he playing saxophone at the time?
